title: Toronto Police officers to stand trial in death of mentally ill man
article: Four Toronto Police officers have been committed to stand trial on manslaughter charges in the beating death of Otto Vass, a mentally ill man who had caused a late-night disturbance at a Toronto convenience store.

Ontario Court Judge Paul Taylor ruled yesterday that sufficient evidence exists to commit Constables Robert LeMaitre, Phillip Duncan, Nam-Nhat Le and Filippo Bevilacqua to trial, but stressed that his decision had no relevance to whether the officers are guilty or innocent of the charges.

The death of Otto Vass on Aug. 9, 2001, in a 7-Eleven parking lot on College Street brought allegations of police brutality. Since that day, dozens of members of the Committee for Justice for Otto Vass have demonstrated at court hearings for the officers.
They were at Old City Hall yesterday, waving a yellow banner on the courthouse steps, while the four officers were hustled out of the back of the building to avoid news cameras.

Judge Taylor said his job in the officers' preliminary hearing was simply to determine whether prosecutors have any evidence on which a jury could infer that the officers unlawfully killed Mr. Vass, who eyewitnesses said was beaten with nightsticks and kicked as he lay on the ground.

"Some judges comment at this point on the strength or weakness of the Crown's case," he said. "I don't intend to do that. How could I possibly comment without having seen the full picture?" including the entire Crown case, any defence evidence, and lawyers' submissions.
Lawyer Gary Clewley, who represents Constable LeMaitre, told reporters on the courthouse steps that the preliminary was "just a warm-up exercise. Don't confuse it with the tennis match."
The judge heard nothing about whether Mr. Vass had a predisposition to violence, Mr. Clewley said, "and that is going to be relevant."

At the time of Mr. Vass's death, neighbours of the 7-Eleven store told local newspapers they saw four policemen fighting with Mr. Vass, and said that officers continued to beat him as he lay motionless on the ground.
The officers are to appear in Ontario Superior Court in late August to set a date for trial.
